hero.title: Xiabu weaving
hero.subtitle: How Wanzai weavers turn ramie fiber into summer cloth

videoHint: Video playback may use significant data — Wi-Fi recommended
paras: Xiabu is a traditional woven ramie cloth. The craft in Wanzai traces its roots to the late Eastern Jin dynasty. Wanzai and Rongchang were listed together in the second group of China’s national intangible cultural heritage entries in 2008.
Weavers prepare the ramie threads, size the warp, set up the loom and weave the cloth. The airy fabric absorbs moisture and is traditionally used for summer clothing.
Xiabu is still made in Jiangxi. The finished fabric can be used in clothing and other textiles.
